{"id": "7de43e88-3d4a-4255-9080-c507724ed8bc", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_E31tTpHvRmRuB4q2fPB1hb", "content": [{"text": "{"iso8601":"2026-09-28T19:35:30.503886+00:00","unix":1790624130.504,"day_of_week":"Monday"}"}], "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_NbI4VOx9o2NDx1tMu1PFJS", "content": [{"text": "     1	---
     2	name: aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation
     3	description: Use this skill for GPU training or inference clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or
     4	  EKS), ParallelCluster, or self-managed EC2/EKS GPU instances. It adds three things.
     5	  First, a GPU evidence coverage audit that proves per node whether kernel Xid logs and
     6	  HyperPod health-agent detections were actually arriving, hour by hour, so "no errors
     7	  found" is never reported from a silent log. Second, a node verdict (replace, reboot,
     8	  or leave alone) against an explicit evidence bar, so an application Xid is never
     9	  headlined as hardware. Third, a pre-flight readiness check before a long run, covering
     10	  Capacity Block or training plan end time versus run length, spare capacity to replace
     11	  a failed node, NodeRecovery, deep health checks, EFA, log coverage, idle reserved
     12	  GPUs. Activate on Xid or ECC errors, slow training or FSx for Lustre slowness on a GPU
     13	  cluster, NCCL hangs or TCP fallback, NVLink or Fabric Manager errors, nodes in Failure
     14	  or Pending, nodes terminating at once, or "is my cluster ready for a multi-day run".
     15	metadata:
     16	  author: nzuresh
     17	  version: "1.0.0"
     18	  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: "Incident RCA, Chat tasks"
     19	  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: "Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, AWS ParallelCluster, Amazon EC2, Amazon FSx for Lustre, Elastic Fabric Adapter, Amazon EKS, AWS Health"
     20	  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: "Machine Learning, GenAI, High Performance Computing"
     21	---
     22	
     23	# GPU Cluster Evidence, Readiness, and Fault Verdicts
     24	
     25	For GPU clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or EKS), AWS ParallelCluster, and self-managed
     26	EC2 or EKS. Generic investigation finds the obvious signals; this skill adds what it gets
     27	wrong: silent evidence, wrong-headline hardware verdicts, and predictable failures before a
     28	long run. **Read-only.** Never reboot, replace, update, or delete anything, and never read
     29	training data, checkpoints, or model weights.
     30	
     31	## Critical rules R1 to R10 (apply in every mode, in this order)
     32	
     33	R1. **Answer in one pass.** In chat, do not stop to ask a question and do not hand off to a
     34	   separate investigation before answering. If an input is missing, use the default (impact
     35	   window: last 24 hours; run length: evaluate 24, 48, and 72 hours), state the assumption,
     36	   and mark dependent checks `Needs input`. For "slow" or performance questions with no
     37	   time given, use the last 72 hours. Offer follow-ups only after the answer.
     38	R2. **Inventory and capability profile.** HyperPod: `sagemaker.DescribeCluster` and
     39	   `ListClusterNodes` (paginate). EC2/ParallelCluster/EKS: `ec2.DescribeInstances`. For every
     40	   GPU instance type: `ec2.DescribeInstanceTypes` (strip HyperPod `ml.`): GPU count,
     41	   `EfaSupported`, `MaximumEfaInterfaces`; per EC2 node, attached `efa`/`efa-only` interfaces.
     42	   Report `<attached> of <max>`, where attached = interfaces with `InterfaceType` `efa` or
     43	   `efa-only` (the primary ENA interface does not count unless it is `efa`). HyperPod nodes
     44	   are not visible to `DescribeInstances`: say so. On NVSwitch types, search every log source
     45	   found under rule R4 for `Started "Nvidia Fabric Manager"` before saying it is not confirmed.
     46	R3. **Node identity survives replacement.** A HyperPod reboot keeps the instance ID; a replace
     47	   gives the node a **new instance ID in the same instance group**, so the current ID will
     48	   never appear in the replace request. Query CloudTrail **by event name, not by instance
     49	   ID**: `cloudtrail.LookupEvents` with `LookupAttributes=[{AttributeKey: EventName,
     50	   AttributeValue: BatchReplaceClusterNodes}]`, then again for `BatchRebootClusterNodes`,
     51	   `BatchDeleteClusterNodes`, and `UpdateCluster`, with `StartTime` = window start minus 6
     52	   hours and `EndTime` = now as full ISO-8601 UTC timestamps, paginating with `NextToken`.
     53	   Keep events whose `requestParameters.clusterName` is this cluster. A `nodeIds` entry
     54	   that is not in the current `ListClusterNodes` output was replaced; the instance group
     55	   whose node has a `LaunchTime` just after that event is the replaced group. That operator
     56	   or automatic call is the explanation for the node going `Pending` (Branch E), not hardware.
     57	R4. **Find every log source by substring, not prefix.** Call `logs.DescribeLogGroups` with
     58	   `logGroupNamePattern` (case-sensitive substring) = the cluster name, then again for
     59	   `kernel`, `messages`, `syslog`, `journal`, and `gpu`, paginating with `nextToken`. Never
     60	   search only `/aws/parallelcluster` or `/aws/sagemaker` prefixes: customer pipelines use
     61	   other names (for example `/aws/<pipeline>/<cluster>/kernel`). Evaluate every source found.
     62	R5. **Prove coverage before any "no errors".** For each node and source: find the stream that
     63	   carries `kernel:` lines, then bin **that exact stream** by hour across the window padded by
     64	   one hour. **Always name the evidence you used: quote the full log group name and the exact
     65	   log stream name for every node in the coverage table, and again in the answer text.** A
     66	   coverage claim without the group and stream it rests on is not auditable, so the operator
     67	   cannot re-run it. Any empty hour means `Not observable` for that hour. First and last event times
     68	   are not proof, and the time of the **last `kernel:` line** is not when logging stopped:
     69	   a healthy kernel goes quiet. Liveness comes only from the hourly bins of all lines in
     70	   that stream. A node is `Measured` if one source passes. HyperPod: a missing
     71	   `SagemakerHealthMonitoringAgent/<group>/<instance-id>` stream means `No HMA detections`
     72	   when the cluster log group is otherwise live. NCCL transport with no `NCCL INFO` lines
     73	   anywhere is `Not observable`; never infer it from the instance type.
     74	R6. **Verdict per node, headline to match.** `REPLACE`, `REBOOT`, `LEAVE ALONE`, `MONITOR`, or
     75	   `NOT OBSERVABLE`, against the evidence bar in `references/incident-branches.md` (Step 4b).
     76	   Application-class Xids (for example 13, 31) or HMA `reason: XidUserAppError` with the node
     77	   `Running` is `LEAVE ALONE`. Never headline "hardware error" unless the verdict is `REPLACE`
     78	   or `REBOOT` on hardware grounds.
     79	R7. **Label every cause** `Proven` (measured signal on the affected node, before the failure,
     80	   nothing competing) or `Hypothesis (to validate)` with the one confirming measurement. A
     81	   spike at the same time is correlation. FSx without a saturated metric is not a proven cause.
     82	   Only a `Proven` cause may be called the root cause, in the headline or in a branch table.
     83	   Otherwise write `Leading hypothesis: <cause>`, or `Root cause: Not observable` when the
     84	   deciding evidence is missing (for example a dead control-plane log). Never write "Proven
     85	   mechanism" for something whose trigger or removal path you did not observe.
     86	   Utilization metrics from FSx (`NetworkThroughputUtilization`, `DiskIopsUtilization`, and
     87	   similar) and `GPUPowerUtilization` are already percent from 0 to 100: a value of `0.9` is
     88	   0.9 percent. Quote the raw value with a percent sign.
     89	R8. **Recovery questions** always state three things: whether automatic node recovery is on
     90	   (`NodeRecovery`), what it does (reboot or replace the node), and that the **job** resumes
     91	   only with checkpoints plus the orchestrator's auto-resume (Slurm on HyperPod:
     92	   `srun --auto-resume=1`).
     93	R9. **Capacity Blocks** begin terminating instances 30 minutes before the end time (60 for
     94	   UltraServers); blocks end at 11:30 UTC and termination starts at 11:00 UTC on the last day.
     95	   For a planned run, write out: usable until = end time minus the lead time; run end = start
     96	   plus run length; hours covered = usable until minus start. Give every value as a full UTC
     97	   date and time, and check the latest safe start is not already in the past.
     98	R10. **Rule out the frequent non-GPU causes** in `references/cluster-edge-cases.md` before
     99	   blaming hardware: subnet IP or network interface exhaustion, ParallelCluster bootstrap
     100	   failures and protected mode, EFA nodes in a public subnet, a Capacity Block not yet
     101	   active, and the FSx maintenance window. HyperPod does not export system metrics to
     102	   CloudWatch, so HyperPod GPU activity is `Not observable` there.
     103	
     104	## Pick the mode
     105	
     106	| The user asks | Mode | Steps to run |
     107	|---------------|------|--------------|
     108	| Something failed, hung, slowed, or lost nodes | **I: Incident** | Steps 1 to 7 |
     109	| "Were there GPU errors?", "Can I trust the logs?" | **C: Coverage audit** | Steps 1 to 3, then 6 and 7 |
     110	| "Is the cluster ready for a long run?", Capacity Block ending | **P: Pre-flight** | Steps 1 to 3, then 5P, 6 and 7 |
     111	
     112	## Workflow checklist
     113	
     114	Work through these in order and tick each one as it completes. Skip only the steps the
     115	mode table excludes. Every step below has a matching `## Step N` section with its detail.
     116	
     117	- [ ] Step 1: Scope the request — account, region, cluster or instance IDs, impact window
     118	- [ ] Step 2: Build the inventory, capability profile, and one ordered timeline
     119	- [ ] Step 3: Prove GPU log coverage per node before looking for errors
     120	- [ ] Step 4: Classify each fault and give every node a verdict
     121	- [ ] Step 5: Pull metrics and settle the root-cause branch
     122	- [ ] Step 5P: Score pre-flight checks P1 to P16 (Mode P only, replaces Steps 4 and 5)
     123	- [ ] Step 6: Write the report in the required format
     124	- [ ] Step 7: Self-check the finished output, then present it
     125	
     126	## Step 1: Scope
     127	
     128	Account, region, cluster name or instance IDs, workload, impact window (default last 24 hours,
     129	stated). Classify the symptom to pick a starting branch (Step 5), but collect evidence for all.
     130	
     131	## Step 2: Inventory and timeline
     132	
     133	Load [references/inventory-and-timeline.md](references/inventory-and-timeline.md) for the
     134	inventory API calls and the seven timeline sources, and
     135	[references/cluster-edge-cases.md](references/cluster-edge-cases.md) for the frequent non-GPU
     136	causes to rule out under rule R10:
     137	
     138	```
     139	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/inventory-and-timeline.md")
     140	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/cluster-edge-cases.md")
     141	```
     142	
     143	Build one ordered timeline for the window plus 30 minutes each side: node state, HMA
     144	detections, Xids, AWS Health, EC2 status and scheduled events, Capacity Block and training plan
     145	end times, and CloudTrail cluster changes (rule R3).
     146	
     147	## Step 3: Coverage audit
     148	
     149	Load [references/coverage-audit.md](references/coverage-audit.md) for the log-source discovery
     150	and hourly coverage queries, and
     151	[references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md](references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md) for NCCL transport, NVLink and
     152	NVSwitch, and EFA signals:
     153	
     154	```
     155	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/coverage-audit.md")
     156	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md")
     157	```
     158	
     159	Produce the coverage table and the node capability and fabric table for every affected node.
     160	Every row names the full log group name and the exact log stream name that row's verdict rests
     161	on, so the operator can re-run the same query. Where no stream carries kernel lines, say which
     162	groups you searched and that none did.
     163	
     164	## Step 4: Classify faults and give node verdicts
     165	
     166	Load [references/xid-triage.md](references/xid-triage.md) for the Xid catalog and per-code
     167	verdicts, and [references/incident-branches.md](references/incident-branches.md) for the node
     168	verdict evidence bar and branches A to F:
     169	
     170	```
     171	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/xid-triage.md")
     172	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/incident-branches.md")
     173	```
     174	
     175	## Step 5: Metrics and root-cause branch
     176	
     177	Load [references/signals-and-thresholds.md](references/signals-and-thresholds.md) for metric
     178	names, dimensions, and thresholds:
     179	
     180	```
     181	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/signals-and-thresholds.md")
     182	```
     183	
     184	Pull FSx (correct dimensions per metric), GPU activity (`AWS/EC2` `GPUPowerUtilization`, unit
     185	Percent, or `CWAgent`), and EFA counters, then evaluate branches A (hardware), B (capacity
     186	lifecycle), C (storage), D (NCCL, NVLink/NVSwitch, EFA), E (cluster change), and F (application,
     187	only after A to E are ruled out), as defined in `incident-branches.md`. Recommend operator
     188	actions only.
     189	
     190	## Step 5P: Pre-flight readiness (Mode P)
     191	
     192	Load [references/preflight.md](references/preflight.md) for pre-flight checks P1 to P16:
     193	
     194	```
     195	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/preflight.md")
     196	```
     197	
     198	Score checks P1 to P16. Lead with FAIL, then RISK. In Mode P this step replaces
     199	Steps 4 and 5.
     200	
     201	## Step 6: Report
     202	
     203	Load [references/report-format.md](references/report-format.md) for the report template and its rules:
     204	
     205	```
     206	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/report-format.md")
     207	```
     208	
     209	## Step 7: Self-check before presenting
     210	
     211	Before showing the answer to the user, re-read your own draft and verify each of these.
     212	Fix the draft where a check fails; do not present an output that fails one.
     213	
     214	- [ ] Every "no errors found" statement is backed by a node whose coverage you proved in
     215	      Step 3. If coverage was not proven, the wording is `Not observable`, not healthy.
     216	- [ ] Every coverage row names its full log group and exact log stream (rule R5). A coverage
     217	      claim with no named source is not auditable and must be fixed before presenting.
     218	- [ ] Every node verdict still meets the evidence bar that justifies it, re-read from
     219	      [references/incident-branches.md](references/incident-branches.md) Step 4b.
     220	- [ ] The headline matches the verdicts. It does not say "hardware error" unless a verdict
     221	      is `REPLACE` or `REBOOT` on hardware grounds (rule R6).
     222	- [ ] Every cause carries a `Proven` or `Hypothesis (to validate)` label, and anything
     223	      labelled `Proven` has a measured signal on the affected node before the failure
     224	      (rule R7). Nothing unproven is called the root cause.
     225	- [ ] Every percentage came straight from the metric without rescaling (rule R7).
     226	- [ ] Every absent signal is reported as `Not observable` with what to collect, never as
     227	      zero or as healthy.
     228	- [ ] Each recommendation names an operator action, and no mutating API call was made.
     229	- [ ] Every number in the answer can be traced to a call you actually made this run.
     230	
     231	State the outcome of this self-check in one line, naming anything you could not verify.
     232	
     233	## Success criteria
     234	
     235	- Coverage table and node capability table for every affected node; no "no errors" without
     236	  proven coverage.
     237	- One verdict per node with a GPU signal; headline consistent with the verdicts.
     238	- Every cause labelled `Proven` or `Hypothesis (to validate)`.
     239	- Replaced nodes matched to the operator or automatic action that replaced them.
     240	- Mode P: P1 to P16 scored.
     241	- No mutating API call was made.
     242	
     243	## References
     244	
     245	- [HyperPod health monitoring system](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sagemaker-hyperpod-eks-resiliency-health-monitoring-agent.html)
     246	- [HyperPod deep health checks](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sagemaker-hyperpod-resiliency-slurm-deep-health-checks.html)
     247	- [Manually replace or reboot a HyperPod node](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sagemaker-hyperpod-resiliency-slurm-replace-faulty-instance.html)
     248	- [HyperPod Slurm cluster logging](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sagemaker-hyperpod-cluster-management-slurm.html)
     249	- [ClusterInstanceStatusDetails](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/APIReference/API_ClusterInstanceStatusDetails.html)
     250	- [How Capacity Blocks work](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/capacity-blocks-how.html)
     251	- [EFA security group requirements](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/efa-start-nccl.html)
     252	- [Monitor Capacity Blocks using EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/capacity-blocks-monitor.html)
     253	- [FSx for Lustre metrics and dimensions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/fs-metrics.html)
     254	- [NVIDIA Xid catalog](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/xid-errors/analyzing-xid-catalog.html)
     255	- [EC2 accelerator metrics (GPUPowerUtilization)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/viewing_metrics_with_cloudwatch.html#accelerator-metrics)
     256	- [DescribeTrainingPlan](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/APIReference/API_DescribeTrainingPlan.html)
     257	- [DescribeCapacityBlockExtensionOfferings](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/APIReference/API_DescribeCapacityBlockExtensionOfferings.html)"}], "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "user_reference": null}

{"id": "34b4db8e-86d4-4373-83c2-37b8ea861725", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_uCRX4bDURWJK5RmkohaqQW", "content": [{"text": "     1	# Signals and Thresholds
     2	
     3	Thresholds here are investigation heuristics for flagging a signal as worth reporting.
     4	They are not AWS service limits. State the observed value, not only the label.
     5	
     6	## HyperPod node state
     7	
     8	Valid `InstanceStatus.Status` values
     9	([ClusterInstanceStatusDetails](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/APIReference/API_ClusterInstanceStatusDetails.html)):
     10	`Running | Failure | Pending | ShuttingDown | SystemUpdating | DeepHealthCheckInProgress | NotFound`.
     11	
     12	| Signal | Flag when |
     13	|--------|-----------|
     14	| Node in `Failure` | Always. Correlate with HMA log for that instance. |
     15	| Node in `Pending` | Longer than 30 minutes: replacement or launch blocked. Check capacity and `LifecycleConfig` logs. |
     16	| Node in `DeepHealthCheckInProgress` | Well past 2 hours. DCGM level 4 alone typically takes about 45 to 90 minutes, and the stress, EFA, and NCCL tests add to it. Check `DeepHealthCheckResults/<id>` streams first |
     17	| `CurrentCount < TargetCount` | Persisting across two inventory reads. |
     18	| `NodeRecovery = None` | Always report. Automatic reboot or replace is disabled. |
     19	| `CurrentImageId != DesiredImageId` | Software update in progress or stalled. |
     20	
     21	## FSx for Lustre (`AWS/FSx`)
     22	
     23	Metric semantics and dimensions:
     24	[FSx for Lustre metrics and dimensions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/fs-metrics.html).
     25	
     26	| Metric (dimensions) | Stat | Flag when | Meaning |
     27	|---------------------|------|-----------|---------|
     28	| `NetworkThroughputUtilization` (FileSystemId, FileServer) | Maximum | ≥ 90% sustained 5+ min | File server network throughput saturated |
     29	| `FileServerDiskThroughputUtilization` (FileSystemId, FileServer) | Maximum | ≥ 90% sustained 5+ min | OSS-to-disk throughput saturated |
     30	| `DiskIopsUtilization` (FileSystemId, StorageTargetId) | Maximum | ≥ 90% sustained 5+ min | OST IOPS saturated (not on Scratch or Persistent HDD) |
     31	| `CPUUtilization` (FileSystemId, FileServer = MDS*) | Maximum | ≥ 90% sustained 5+ min | Metadata server saturated |
     32	| `MetadataOperations` (FileSystemId) | Sum / period | Sharp rise aligned with the slowdown | Metadata-heavy workload |
     33	| `FreeDataStorageCapacity` (FileSystemId, StorageTargetId) | Minimum per OST | Any OST < 10% free while others have space | Imbalanced striping, write failures possible |
     34	| `DataReadBytes` + `DataWriteBytes` (FileSystemId) | Sum / period | Drop aligned with the stall | Clients stopped doing I/O (effect, not cause) |
     35	
     36	Throughput in bytes per second is `Sum / period_seconds`. Do not report raw `Sum` as a
     37	rate.
     38	
     39	A drop in client I/O during a hang is usually the **effect** of the job stalling. It
     40	points at storage only if a saturation metric above rose first.
     41	
     42	## GPU activity
     43	
     44	`AWS/EC2` `GPUPowerUtilization` (dimensions `InstanceId` and `GpuId`, as observed in live
     45	accounts; the EC2 docs list the metric but not the `GpuId` dimension) is published by EC2 for a

## FINDINGS: GPU-activity and EFA/network metric observability in CloudWatch for the HyperPod nodes

**Account 111122223333, region us-west-2. Window 2026-09-25T16:00:00Z → 2026-09-28T19:35:00Z (current time 2026-09-28T19:40:00Z).**

### HyperPod GPU node inventory (from `sagemaker.ListClusterNodes`)
- `skilltest-hp-slurm`: `gpu-g5-2xl` = **i-0a1fb336e15f3b9e2** (Running); `gpu-g5-xl` = **i-0e33004a2943acd24** (Running); plus `controller` i-02715ec68a2c15277.
- `skilltest-hp-eks-hp`: `gpu-g5-4xlarge` = **i-02624d38db12cb999** (Running).

### Task 1 — AWS/EC2 GPUPowerUtilization
`cloudwatch.ListMetrics` (Namespace AWS/EC2, MetricName GPUPowerUtilization) **returns metrics — but NOT for any HyperPod node.** They exist for six unrelated instance IDs (i-0190035035290b380, i-0a3cfc5c0505eb807, i-0014ff22f2e2f180f, i-0be6193831c898671, i-01ec042d2f0e3e7fb, i-0ce092c23d7562556), each with `GpuId` **1–8** (8 GPUs per instance). That GpuId 1–8 pattern is inconsistent with the single-A10G g5.xlarge/2xlarge/4xlarge HyperPod nodes, confirming these are different (multi-GPU) instances.
- `GetMetricData` for the three real HyperPod node IDs → **0 data points each** (empty `Values`, StatusCode Complete). **GPUPowerUtilization is NOT observable for the HyperPod nodes.**
- (For context, sampling one of the *unrelated* IDs, i-0014ff22f2e2f180f, returned 516 points ranging min 0.0018% to max 0.0050% — raw percent-of-max-active-power values; but this instance is not part of either HyperPod cluster and is out of scope.)

### Task 2 — CWAgent (nvidia_smi_*, efa_*, node_amazonefa_*)
`cloudwatch.ListMetrics` (Namespace CWAgent) returns only **disk_used_percent** and **mem_used_percent** for a single instance (i-08a11867e0b7e311d — not a HyperPod node). **None** of the requested metrics exist anywhere in CWAgent: no `nvidia_smi_utilization_gpu`, no `nvidia_smi_memory_used/total`, no `nvidia_smi_utilization_memory`, and **no `efa_*` or `node_amazonefa_*` counters** (no retransmits, timeouts, impaired/unresponsive-remote, or work-request-error counters). **GPU-utilization and GPU-memory via CWAgent = Not observable. EFA/network counters = Not observable.**

### Task 3 — Other custom namespaces
Full unfiltered `ListMetrics` surfaced these non-AWS-standard namespaces: **`FsxTrainingObservability`**, **`AWS/Prometheus`**, `CWAgent`, `ParallelCluster`, `/aws/sagemaker/Clusters`, `ECSMCPService/Tools`.
- **`FsxTrainingObservability`**: only `mem_used_percent` and `disk_used_percent` (path /dev/shm) for three IDs (i-01bbde10b04dd4ca8, i-0be6193831c898671, i-0014ff22f2e2f180f). **No GPU or EFA metrics**, and these IDs are **not** the HyperPod GPU nodes.
- **`AWS/Prometheus`**: only AMP workspace *service* metrics (OutOfOrderSampleAge, QuerySamplesProcessed, RuleGroup/RuleEvaluation… for workspace `ws-b2a9f25a-ce3b-4aea-9cd4-8356ba7b9d57`). These are AMP internal operational metrics, **not** GPU/EFA time series. There is an AMP workspace present (rule group named `distributed-training-triage-b200…`), but **no DCGM/GPU or EFA telemetry is mirrored into CloudWatch** — any such data would live inside AMP, not queryable here.

### Task 4 — GetMetricData
No GPU-activity or EFA metric exists for any HyperPod node, so there is nothing to trend. The only GPUPowerUtilization series with data belong to out-of-scope, non-HyperPod instances.

## DELIVERABLE — Observable vs Not observable (for the three HyperPod GPU nodes)

| Metric class | Source checked | Result for HyperPod nodes |
|---|---|---|
| GPU activity — GPUPowerUtilization | AWS/EC2 | **Not observable** (0 data points for i-0a1fb336e15f3b9e2, i-0e33004a2943acd24, i-02624d38db12cb999) |
| GPU utilization / memory — nvidia_smi_* | CWAgent | **Not observable** (metrics absent entirely) |
| GPU utilization / memory — DCGM | FsxTrainingObservability / AWS/Prometheus (CW) | **Not observable** (no GPU series mirrored to CloudWatch) |
| EFA / network counters — efa_* / node_amazonefa_* | CWAgent (and all namespaces) | **Not observable** (metrics absent entirely) |

**Bottom line:** For the two SageMaker HyperPod clusters' GPU nodes, **neither GPU-activity metrics nor EFA/network counters are observable in CloudWatch.** This matches skill rule R10: *HyperPod does not export system metrics to CloudWatch.* The GPUPowerUtilization and CWAgent/FsxTrainingObservability series that do exist belong to other, non-HyperPod instances and must **not** be attributed to these clusters — and an absent metric must **never** be read as 0% utilization.

**The GPU/network-vs-storage question therefore cannot be answered from CloudWatch metrics.** It must be answered from logs (kernel Xid lines, HyperPod health-agent detections, NCCL logs — per the coverage audit) and/or from Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus directly (the AMP workspace `ws-b2a9f25a-ce3b-4aea-9cd4-8356ba7b9d57` may hold DCGM/EFA series not mirrored to CloudWatch). To make GPU activity observable in CloudWatch would require the CloudWatch agent with the NVIDIA/DCGM plugin on the nodes, or the HyperPod observability add-on exporting to AMP with a CloudWatch mirror. Note also: EFA is not supported on g5.xlarge/2xlarge/4xlarge, so EFA/NCCL inter-node transport is largely not applicable regardless.

**Caveat / not verified:** whether the AMP workspace actually contains GPU/EFA series for these specific nodes was not queried (only its CloudWatch-side service metrics were visible); confirming that would require querying AMP directly.

Maps to Branch B (capacity) - end-of-reservation reclaim. The reclaimed capacity was in us-west-2d; place replacement capacity in an AZ the cluster subnets can launch into.\n\n*Create a launch-template version targeting the new active reservation, overriding only CapacityReservationTarget; record the new version number.*\n\n```bash\naws ec2 create-launch-template-version --region us-west-2 --launch-template-id lt-025a88cbeaba7b869 --source-version 1 --version-description \"Point GPU compute at newly acquired active Capacity Block\" --launch-template-data '{\"CapacityReservationSpecification\":{\"CapacityReservationTarget\":{\"CapacityReservationId\":\"<new-capacity-reservation-id>\"}}}'\n```\n\n**Advisory:**\n- If you took the on-demand fallback, also override InstanceMarketOptions to remove capacity-block so instances launch on-demand.\n\n*Make the new version the default so Slurm launches GPU nodes against active reserved capacity, not a deleted reservation.*\n\n```bash\naws ec2 modify-launch-template --region us-west-2 --launch-template-id lt-025a88cbeaba7b869 --default-version <new-version-number>\n```\n\n**Advisory:**\n- Confirm the ParallelCluster compute-resource references the LT default (or intended) version; if it pins a specific version, update via pcluster update-cluster. Then resume the Slurm partition so the fleet scales back to the reserved size.\n\n*Create an EventBridge rule on Capacity Block Expiration Warning routed to on-call, so operators get ahead of the next reservation ending (no such rule exists today).*\n\n```bash\naws events put-rule --region us-west-2 --name capacity-block-expiration-warning-distributed-training-triage-b200 --state ENABLED --description \"Notify on EC2 Capacity Block Expiration Warning\" --event-pattern '{\"source\":[\"aws.ec2\"],\"detail-type\":[\"Capacity Block Expiration Warning\"]}' && aws events put-targets --region us-west-2 --rule capacity-block-expiration-warning-distributed-training-triage-b200 --targets 'Id=1,Arn=<your-ops-sns-topic-arn>'\n```\n\n**Advisory:**\n- Capacity Blocks begin terminating instances 30 min before end (60 min for UltraServers); blocks end 11:30 UTC with termination starting 11:00 UTC on the last day. Parameterize the compute-resource CapacityReservationTarget and the queue TargetCount/MaxCount to the active reservation and its size, add a runbook step to re-point on renewal/repurchase, and consider an on-demand fallback path in config.\n\nAcceptance criteria:\n- The capacity reservation target is a parameter, not a literal ID in config.\n- The GPU queue TargetCount/MaxCount matches the acquired reserved instance count.\n- A deploy against a stale/deleted reservation is detected (validation/drift check) rather than silently failing at RunInstances time.\n\n**2. # Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### B200 training throughput declined to ~zero over several days
**Description:** Aggregate GPU training throughput on the ParallelCluster distributed-training-triage-b200 fleet (p6-b200.48xlarge) reading its dataset from FSx for Lustre fs-077c776983688ad76 declined over ~72h and reached effectively zero. The fleet stepped down 6->2 nodes by 2026-09-23 and dropped to zero at 2026-09-27 ~11:00Z.
**Time:** 2026-09-25T16:00:00Z - 2026-09-27T11:00:00Z

## Findings

### Cause: B200 compute fleet dropped to zero at 2026-09-27 ~11:00Z
**Description:** The two remaining p6-b200.48xlarge nodes (gpu-st-p6b20048xlarge-1 = i-0be6193831c898671, -2 = i-0014ff22f2e2f180f) emitted normal telemetry (computemgtd heartbeats, SSM credential rotation, systemd) until 2026-09-27T10:59:54Z, then went silent in the same second with no shutdown/panic/Xid - an external hard-termination. Host metrics stopped ~10:55Z and AMP ingest collapsed ~87x (435->5 samples/eval) over 11:00-11:15Z. Earlier-gen nodes had already been retired 2026-09-23 15:52Z (cluster-managed TerminateInstances), so the fleet was 6->2 before this final stop.
**Cascades to:** symptom-throughput

### Cause: Slurm could not replace the lost nodes (reservation inactive)
**Description:** After the node loss, ParallelCluster/Slurm resume issued RunInstances at 11:17/11:18/11:19Z which all failed with 'Capacity Reservation cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b is not active'. With no valid capacity in any launch-template version, the outage could not self-heal and the fleet stayed at zero GPUs.
**Cascades to:** symptom-throughput

### Root Cause: Capacity Block cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b ended, terminating the B200 fleet with no replacement possible
**Description:** ROOT CAUSE. The p6-b200.48xlarge fleet ran on EC2 Capacity Block cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b (launch template lt-025a88cbeaba7b869, MarketType capacity-block). The reservation ended and AWS reclaimed the last two nodes at 2026-09-27T10:59:54Z (clean telemetry to the instant, no Xid/ECC/NVLink fault, no customer TerminateInstances in the window - the AWS end-of-reservation reclaim signature). ParallelCluster/Slurm then attempted replacement RunInstances at 11:17/11:18/11:19Z, all rejected with 'Client.InvalidParameterValue: Capacity Reservation cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b is not active'. Both Capacity Blocks referenced by the launch template are now deleted (cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b on versions 2/3/4 and cr-0884d02f8b1b344e5 on default version 1 both return NotFound), so no LT version points at valid capacity and the fleet stayed at zero. Maps to Branch B (capacity) - end-of-reservation reclaim. Ruled out: hardware (no Xid/ECC/NVLink), bootstrap failure, protected mode, health-check self-termination, idle scale-down (no slurm_suspend), and manual termination.
**Cascades to:** finding-fleet-stop, finding-no-replacement

### Hypothesis: Storage (FSx for Lustre) ruled out
**Description:** FSx fs-077c776983688ad76 (SCRATCH_2, 1200 GiB) was healthy and barely used across the window: peak DataReadBytes ~13.6 B/s vs a ~234 MB/s baseline; NetworkThroughputUtilization ~0.04%, disk throughput ~0.13%, MDT DiskIopsUtilization ~0.12%, MDS CPU <=7.6% peak; single OST (imbalance impossible); free capacity flat; no in-window maintenance. Not throughput-, IOPS-, metadata-, or capacity-bound. Storage is not the cause. The ClientConnections 15->5 step at 2026-09-28 00:00Z is downstream (~13h after all GPU compute had already stopped), not a trigger.
**Cascades to:** symptom-throughput

#### Gaps
- **GPU/EFA/NVLink health series unreachable in-window:** GPU/network health for the B200 fleet is not directly observable from reachable tooling: (1) AWS/EC2 GPUPowerUtilization exists (used as an activity proxy) but the rich DCGM/EFA/NVLink/LNet/ECC series live only in AMP workspace ws-b2a9f25a (fsx-training-correlator), reachable solely via the AMP Prometheus HTTP query API (not a boto3 op) - an operator must run PromQL directly; (2) kernel-facility log shipping to the b200 kernel log group stopped 2026-09-24T19:29Z (a day before the window), so Xid/ECC visibility is absent in-window - a GPU hardware fault is Not observable (no evidence, and GPUs were idle); (3) AMP has no scraper - ingestion is node-agent remote-write that collapsed when the nodes died.
- **Deleted Capacity Block's exact end time not directly readable:** cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b is deleted (InvalidCapacityReservationId.NotFound), so its scheduled end time cannot be read directly. Its type is confirmed as a Capacity Block via the launch template's MarketType=capacity-block; the ~11:00Z reclaim and 'is not active' error are strong evidence of end-of-reservation reclaim.
- **Head-node Slurm control-plane logs dark since 2026-08-31:** The b200 head node clustermgtd/slurmctld CloudWatch streams stopped ingesting on 2026-08-31 (~4 weeks before the incident), so there is no on-head control-plane record of the 09-27 node loss or the exact Slurm resume error text. Evidence was reconstructed from compute-node telemetry + CloudTrail. The head node and its IAM role are intact (it authenticated the failed RunInstances).

# Mitigation Summary

## Action
Restore GPU capacity to ParallelCluster distributed-training-triage-b200: acquire a new active Capacity Block (or ODCR / on-demand fallback), re-point launch template lt-025a88cbeaba7b869 at it and make it default, add a Capacity Block Expiration Warning alert, and repair the observability pipeline (kernel-log shipping, AMP ingestion, clustermgtd/slurmctld logging).

## Reasoning
The p6-b200.48xlarge fleet ran on Capacity Block cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b, which ended; AWS hard-terminated the last two nodes at 2026-09-27T10:59:54Z and every Slurm RunInstances replacement failed with 'Capacity Reservation cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b is not active', driving GPU throughput to zero. No active reserved capacity exists (both cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b and cr-0884d02f8b1b344e5 return NotFound; all launch-template versions 1-4 target a deleted Capacity Block), so capacity must be re-acquired, not merely re-pointed. ## Code Change Specification

### Requirements

#### 1. Track active reserved capacity in ParallelCluster IaC instead of pinning a fixed reservation ID
**Description:** Every version of lt-025a88cbeaba7b869 hard-codes a now-deleted reservation ID. Parameterize the compute-resource CapacityReservationTarget and the queue TargetCount/MaxCount to the active reservation and its size, add a runbook step to re-point on renewal/repurchase, and consider an on-demand fallback path in config.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- The capacity reservation target is a parameter, not a literal ID in config.
- The GPU queue TargetCount/MaxCount matches the acquired reserved instance count.
- A deploy against a stale/deleted reservation is detected (validation/drift check) rather than silently failing at RunInstances time.

#### 2. Get ahead of Capacity Block expiry so the job checkpoints and capacity is renewed before end
**Description:** Codify the EventBridge Capacity Block Expiration Warning rule and target in IaC, add a pre-run readiness check comparing the block end time (minus 30-min lead, 60 for UltraServers) against planned run length, and add automated checkpointing keyed to the reservation end.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- The expiration-warning rule and target are defined in IaC and deployed with the cluster.
- A readiness check fails when run length exceeds usable-until (end time minus lead).
- Checkpoint cadence guarantees a recoverable checkpoint before the reservation end.

#### 3. Make the observability pipeline durable so future starvation or node loss is caught
**Description:** Codify: (1) kernel-facility log collection to the kernel log group so Xids are captured; (2) clustermgtd/slurmctld shipping to the slurm log group; (3) an AMP ingestion path that survives compute-node loss; (4) an alarm on sustained low GPUPowerUtilization / near-zero FSx read throughput so a starved fleet is flagged.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- CloudWatch agent ships the kernel facility and Slurm control-plane logs, verified by fresh events in both log groups.
- AMP keeps receiving DCGM/EFA/NVLink/LNet series via a collector that survives node termination.
- An alarm fires on sustained near-zero GPU utilization or near-zero FSx read throughput.

# FSx for Lustre `fs-077c776983688ad76` — Storage Saturation Analysis

## Verdict: Storage is NOT saturated. FSx is NOT the cause of the training throughput drop.

Every saturation dimension of this file system is essentially idle throughout the entire 72h window. This FSx file system is not throughput-bound, not disk-IOPS-bound, not metadata/MDS-CPU-bound, and not capacity/OST-imbalance-bound. In fact the file system is barely being used at all — the client-side I/O numbers show the training job is reading almost nothing from FSx.

## Dimension discovery (ListMetrics, AWS/FSx, FileSystemId=fs-077c776983688ad76)

{"id": "8b345736-86f9-4eb2-ac72-b2f65f5c00e2", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_zsEu3S4AF4XkRoEzylEuB6", "content": [{"text": "Successfully loaded /aidevops/skills/system/exploring-metrics/SKILL.md"}], "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_FF4amdDUBT0kHylYWyIT4m", "content": [{"text": "     1	---
     2	name: aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation

     12	  GPUs. Activate on Xid or ECC errors, slow training or FSx for Lustre slowness on a GPU
     13	  cluster, NCCL hangs or TCP fallback, NVLink or Fabric Manager errors, nodes in Failure

     15	metadata:
     16	  author: nzuresh
     17	  version: "1.0.0"
     18	  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: "Incident RCA, Chat tasks"
     19	  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: "Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, AWS ParallelCluster, Amazon EC2, Amazon FSx for Lustre, Elastic Fabric Adapter, Amazon EKS, AWS Health"
     20	  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: "Machine Learning, GenAI, High Performance Computing"
     21	---
     22	
     23	# GPU Cluster Evidence, Readiness, and Fault Verdicts
     24	
     25	For GPU clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or EKS), AWS ParallelCluster, and self-managed
     26	EC2 or EKS. Generic investigation finds the obvious signals; this skill adds what it gets
     27	wrong: silent evidence, wrong-headline hardware verdicts, and predictable failures before a
     28	long run. **Read-only.** Never reboot, replace, update, or delete anything, and never read
     29	training data, checkpoints, or model weights.
     30	
     31	## Critical rules R1 to R10 (apply in every mode, in this order)
     32	
     33	R1. **Answer in one pass.** In chat, do not stop to ask a question and do not hand off to a
     34	   separate investigation before answering. If an input is missing, use the default (impact
     35	   window: last 24 hours; run length: evaluate 24, 48, and 72 hours), state the assumption,
     36	   and mark dependent checks `Needs input`. For "slow" or performance questions with no
     37	   time given, use the last 72 hours. Offer follow-ups only after the answer.
     38	R2. **Inventory and capability profile.** HyperPod: `sagemaker.DescribeCluster` and
     39	   `ListClusterNodes` (paginate). EC2/ParallelCluster/EKS: `ec2.DescribeInstances`. For every
     40	   GPU instance type: `ec2.DescribeInstanceTypes` (strip HyperPod `ml.`): GPU count,
     41	   `EfaSupported`, `MaximumEfaInterfaces`; per EC2 node, attached `efa`/`efa-only` interfaces.
     42	   Report `<attached> of <max>`, where attached = interfaces with `InterfaceType` `efa` or
     43	   `efa-only` (the primary ENA interface does not count unless it is `efa`). HyperPod nodes
     44	   are not visible to `DescribeInstances`: say so. On NVSwitch types, search every log source
     45	   found under rule R4 for `Started "Nvidia Fabric Manager"` before saying it is not confirmed.
     46	R3. **Node identity survives replacement.** A HyperPod reboot keeps the instance ID; a replace
     47	   gives the node a **new instance ID in the same instance group**, so the current ID will
     48	   never appear in the replace request. Query CloudTrail **by event name, not by instance
     49	   ID**: `cloudtrail.LookupEvents` with `LookupAttributes=[{AttributeKey: EventName,
     50	   AttributeValue: BatchReplaceClusterNodes}]`, then again for `BatchRebootClusterNodes`,
     51	   `BatchDeleteClusterNodes`, and `UpdateCluster`, with `StartTime` = window start minus 6
     52	   hours and `EndTime` = now as full ISO-8601 UTC timestamps, paginating with `NextToken`.
     53	   Keep events whose `requestParameters.clusterName` is this cluster. A `nodeIds` entry
     54	   that is not in the current `ListClusterNodes` output was replaced; the instance group
     55	   whose node has a `LaunchTime` just after that event is the replaced group. That operator
     56	   or automatic call is the explanation for the node going `Pending` (Branch E), not hardware.
     57	R4. **Find every log source by substring, not prefix.** Call `logs.DescribeLogGroups` with
     58	   `logGroupNamePattern` (case-sensitive substring) = the cluster name, then again for
     59	   `kernel`, `messages`, `syslog`, `journal`, and `gpu`, paginating with `nextToken`. Never
     60	   search only `/aws/parallelcluster` or `/aws/sagemaker` prefixes: customer pipelines use
     61	   other names (for example `/aws/<pipeline>/<cluster>/kernel`). Evaluate every source found.
     62	R5. **Prove coverage before any "no errors".** For each node and source: find the stream that
     63	   carries `kernel:` lines, then bin **that exact stream** by hour across the window padded by
     64	   one hour. **Always name the evidence you used: quote the full log group name and the exact
     65	   log stream name for every node in the coverage table, and again in the answer text.** A
     66	   coverage claim without the group and stream it rests on is not auditable, so the operator
     67	   cannot re-run it. Any empty hour means `Not observable` for that hour. First and last event times
     68	   are not proof, and the time of the **last `kernel:` line** is not when logging stopped:
     69	   a healthy kernel goes quiet. Liveness comes only from the hourly bins of all lines in
     70	   that stream. A node is `Measured` if one source passes. HyperPod: a missing
     71	   `SagemakerHealthMonitoringAgent/<group>/<instance-id>` stream means `No HMA detections`
     72	   when the cluster log group is otherwise live. NCCL transport with no `NCCL INFO` lines
     73	   anywhere is `Not observable`; never infer it from the instance type.
     74	R6. **Verdict per node, headline to match.** `REPLACE`, `REBOOT`, `LEAVE ALONE`, `MONITOR`, or
     75	   `NOT OBSERVABLE`, against the evidence bar in `references/incident-branches.md` (Step 4b).
     76	   Application-class Xids (for example 13, 31) or HMA `reason: XidUserAppError` with the node
     77	   `Running` is `LEAVE ALONE`. Never headline "hardware error" unless the verdict is `REPLACE`
     78	   or `REBOOT` on hardware grounds.
     79	R7. **Label every cause** `Proven` (measured signal on the affected node, before the failure,
     80	   nothing competing) or `Hypothesis (to validate)` with the one confirming measurement. A
     81	   spike at the same time is correlation. FSx without a saturated metric is not a proven cause.
     82	   Only a `Proven` cause may be called the root cause, in the headline or in a branch table.
     83	   Otherwise write `Leading hypothesis: <cause>`, or `Root cause: Not observable` when the
     84	   deciding evidence is missing (for example a dead control-plane log). Never write "Proven
     85	   mechanism" for something whose trigger or removal path you did not observe.
     86	   Utilization metrics from FSx (`NetworkThroughputUtilization`, `DiskIopsUtilization`, and
     87	   similar) and `GPUPowerUtilization` are already percent from 0 to 100: a value of `0.9` is
     88	   0.9 percent. Quote the raw value with a percent sign.
     89	R8. **Recovery questions** always state three things: whether automatic node recovery is on
     90	   (`NodeRecovery`), what it does (reboot or replace the node), and that the **job** resumes
     91	   only with checkpoints plus the orchestrator's auto-resume (Slurm on HyperPod:
     92	   `srun --auto-resume=1`).
     93	R9. **Capacity Blocks** begin terminating instances 30 minutes before the end time (60 for
     94	   UltraServers); blocks end at 11:30 UTC and termination starts at 11:00 UTC on the last day.
     95	   For a planned run, write out: usable until = end time minus the lead time; run end = start
     96	   plus run length; hours covered = usable until minus start. Give every value as a full UTC
     97	   date and time, and check the latest safe start is not already in the past.
     98	R10. **Rule out the frequent non-GPU causes** in `references/cluster-edge-cases.md` before
     99	   blaming hardware: subnet IP or network interface exhaustion, ParallelCluster bootstrap
     100	   failures and protected mode, EFA nodes in a public subnet, a Capacity Block not yet
     101	   active, and the FSx maintenance window. HyperPod does not export system metrics to
     102	   CloudWatch, so HyperPod GPU activity is `Not observable` there.
     103	
     104	## Pick the mode
     105	
     106	| The user asks | Mode | Steps to run |
     107	|---------------|------|--------------|
     108	| Something failed, hung, slowed, or lost nodes | **I: Incident** | Steps 1 to 7 |
     109	| "Were there GPU errors?", "Can I trust the logs?" | **C: Coverage audit** | Steps 1 to 3, then 6 and 7 |
     110	| "Is the cluster ready for a long run?", Capacity Block ending | **P: Pre-flight** | Steps 1 to 3, then 5P, 6 and 7 |
     111	
     112	## Workflow checklist
     113	
     114	Work through these in order and tick each one as it completes. Skip only the steps the
     115	mode table excludes. Every step below has a matching `## Step N` section with its detail.
     116

     22	
     23	# GPU Cluster Evidence, Readiness, and Fault Verdicts
     24	
     25	For GPU clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or EKS), AWS ParallelCluster, and self-managed
     26	EC2 or EKS. Generic investigation finds the obvious signals; this skill adds what it gets
     27	wrong: silent evidence, wrong-headline hardware verdicts, and predictable failures before a
     28	long run. **Read-only.** Never reboot, replace, update, or delete anything, and never read
     29	training data, checkpoints, or model weights.
     30	
     31	## Critical rules R1 to R10 (apply in every mode, in this order)
     32	
     33	R1. **Answer in one pass.** In chat, do not stop to ask a question and do not hand off to a
     34	   separate investigation before answering. If an input is missing, use the default (impact
     35	   window: last 24 hours; run length: evaluate 24, 48, and 72 hours), state the assumption,
     36	   and mark dependent checks `Needs input`. For "slow" or performance questions with no
     37	   time given, use the last 72 hours. Offer follow-ups only after the answer.
     38	R2. **Inventory and capability profile.** HyperPod: `sagemaker.DescribeCluster` and
     39	   `ListClusterNodes` (paginate). EC2/ParallelCluster/EKS: `ec2.DescribeInstances`. For every
     40	   GPU instance type: `ec2.DescribeInstanceTypes` (strip HyperPod `ml.`): GPU count,
     41	   `EfaSupported`, `MaximumEfaInterfaces`; per EC2 node, attached `efa`/`efa-only` interfaces.
     42	   Report `<attached> of <max>`, where attached = interfaces with `InterfaceType` `efa` or
     43	   `efa-only` (the primary ENA interface does not count unless it is `efa`). HyperPod nodes
     44	   are not visible to `DescribeInstances`: say so. On NVSwitch types, search every log source
     45	   found under rule R4 for `Started "Nvidia Fabric Manager"` before saying it is not confirmed.
     46	R3. **Node identity survives replacement.** A HyperPod reboot keeps the instance ID; a replace
     47	   gives the node a **new instance ID in the same instance group**, so the current ID will
     48	   never appear in the replace request. Query CloudTrail **by event name, not by instance
     49	   ID**: `cloudtrail.LookupEvents` with `LookupAttributes=[{AttributeKey: EventName,
     50	   AttributeValue: BatchReplaceClusterNodes}]`, then again for `BatchRebootClusterNodes`,
     51	   `BatchDeleteClusterNodes`, and `UpdateCluster`, with `StartTime` = window start minus 6
     52	   hours and `EndTime` = now as full ISO-8601 UTC timestamps, paginating with `NextToken`.
     53	   Keep events whose `requestParameters.clusterName` is this cluster. A `nodeIds` entry
     54	   that is not in the current `ListClusterNodes` output was replaced; the instance group
     55	   whose node has a `LaunchTime` just after that event is the replaced group. That operator
     56	   or automatic call is the explanation for the node going `Pending` (Branch E), not hardware.

     58	   `logGroupNamePattern` (case-sensitive substring) = the cluster name, then again for

     61	   other names (for example `/aws/<pipeline>/<cluster>/kernel`). Evaluate every source found.

     65	   log stream name for every node in the coverage table, and again in the answer text.** A

     68	   are not proof, and the time of the **last `kernel:` line** is not when logging stopped:

     81	   spike at the same time is correlation. FSx without a saturated metric is not a proven cause.

     2	
     3	<!-- Loaded by SKILL.md. Content validated live against HyperPod Slurm, HyperPod EKS, and ParallelCluster clusters. -->
     4	
     5	## Step 3a: Find the kernel log source and prove it covers the nodes
     6	
     7	Xids are only as visible as the customer's log shipping. Locate the source for the
     8	orchestrator, then prove it is actually capturing kernel messages from the affected
     9	nodes before you trust a zero.
     10	
     11	| Orchestrator | Where Xids can appear in CloudWatch Logs |
     12	|--------------|------------------------------------------|
     13	| HyperPod (Slurm or EKS) | HMA detections in `/aws/sagemaker/Clusters/<ClusterName>/<ClusterId>`. The per-node detection stream appears only after the first detection, so it is absent on healthy nodes. HyperPod does not ship the full kernel log. Also check any customer-shipped kernel log group (below). |
     14	| AWS ParallelCluster 3 | `/aws/parallelcluster/<cluster-name>-<timestamp>`, streams `<hostname>.<instance-id>.system-messages` (`/var/log/messages`, Amazon Linux and RHEL) or `<hostname>.<instance-id>.syslog` (`/var/log/syslog`, Ubuntu). Present only when the cluster's CloudWatch logging is on. |
     15	| Self-managed EC2, EKS, or custom pipelines | Whatever group the customer's CloudWatch agent, Fluent Bit, or similar ships `/var/log/messages`, `/var/log/syslog`, the journal, or `dmesg` to. There is no fixed name. |
     16	
     17	How to find customer-shipped groups:
     18	
     19	1. `logs.DescribeLogGroups` with `logGroupNamePattern` (a case-sensitive **substring**
     20	   match, so it finds `/aws/<anything>/<cluster-name>/kernel`), paginated with `nextToken`.
     21	   Run it once for the cluster name, then once each for `kernel`, `messages`, `syslog`,
     22	   `system`, `dmesg`, `journal`, and `gpu`. Do **not** rely on `logGroupNamePrefix` alone:
     23	   customer pipelines rarely use the `/aws/parallelcluster` or `/aws/sagemaker` prefix.
     24	   If the account has few log groups, list them all instead.
     25	2. For each candidate, `logs.DescribeLogStreams` ordered by `LastEventTime`. Keep the
     26	   group if stream names contain the affected **instance IDs** or their private DNS
     27	   hostnames. ParallelCluster and most agents put one or the other in the stream name.
     28	3. Evaluate **every** candidate source before deciding, not just the first one found. A
     29	   node is `Measured` if any one source passes both coverage checks below.
     30	4. If nothing matches, report kernel logs as `Not observable` and name where the operator
     31	   should look. Do not assume there are none.
     32	
     33	**Coverage proof, required before reporting "no Xids":** a healthy kernel is quiet, so
     34	"no kernel lines in the window" does **not** mean the log isn't shipped, and "some
     35	kernel lines" does **not** mean it is. Prove two things per affected instance and per
     36	source.
     37	
     38	**(b) first: find the stream that carries kernel messages from this node.** Run over
     39	the node's lifetime (since launch), not only the window:
     40	
     41	```
     42	filter @logStream like /<instance-id>/ and @message like /kernel:/
     43	| stats count(*) as kernelLines, max(@timestamp) as lastKernelLine by @logStream
     44	```
     45	
     46	(`kernel:` is the syslog-format marker in `/var/log/messages`, `/var/log/syslog`, and
     47	syslog-format journal forwarding. If the source ships the journal as JSON, filter on
     48	its kernel transport field instead.) The `@logStream` values returned are the only
     49	streams that can prove kernel coverage. `NVRM` lines among them (for example the
     50	driver load banner at boot) additionally prove the NVIDIA driver's output reaches
     51	this source. No rows means this source does not carry kernel messages for the node.
     52	
     53	**(a) then: prove that exact stream was continuously live through the impact window.**
     54	Filter on the exact stream name from (b), never on the instance ID alone. On
     55	ParallelCluster the instance ID matches every stream for the node (`slurmd`,
     56	`cloud-init`, `computemgtd`, and others), which makes a dead kernel stream look live.
     57	Bin the padded window (start minus 1 hour, end plus 1 hour) by hour:
     58	
     59	```
     60	filter @logStream = "<exact stream name from (b)>"
     61	| stats count(*) as lines by bin(1h) as hour
     62	| sort hour asc
     63	```
     64	
     65	Live means every hour in the padded window has `lines > 0`. A syslog stream on a
     66	running host normally carries systemd and agent lines every hour, so an empty hour is
     67	a delivery gap. First and last event times alone are **not** proof: a stream can have
     68	events at both ends and nothing in between. List every empty hour in the report.
     69	
     70	**Other GPU-communication signals.** In the same pass, record per node whether each of
     71	these is observable, using `references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md`: NCCL transport lines, Fabric
     72	Manager start lines (NVSwitch instances), `efa_*` or `node_amazonefa_*` counters, and GPU
     73	activity (`GPUPowerUtilization` or `CWAgent`). Each goes in the coverage table as
     74	`Observable`, `Not observable`, or `Not applicable`. A missing signal is a gap to report,
     75	never a clean result.
     76	
     77	**HyperPod is different.** HyperPod does not ship the node's system log. The
     78	health-monitoring agent watches it on the node and writes only **detections**, and the
     79	CloudWatch stream for a node is created only when the first detection is written. A
     80	healthy GPU node therefore has **no** `SagemakerHealthMonitoringAgent/<group>/<instance-id>`
     81	stream. Treat
     82	that as `No HMA detections`, not `Not observable`, provided that:
     83	
     84	- the node is a GPU or Trainium instance (HMA runs on these by default), and
     85	- the cluster log group is receiving other streams, such as `ClusterMetrics/slurm` or
     86	  `LifecycleConfig/...`, so log delivery from the cluster is working.
     87	
     88	If the log group has no streams at all, report HMA status as `Not observable` and ask
     89	the operator to confirm on the node that `sagemaker-health-monitoring-agent.service`
     90	is running. Queries (a) and (b) above do not apply to HMA streams.
     91	
     92	Interpret the results as follows:
     93	
     94	| (a) live across window | (b) kernel lines ever | Xid status to report |
     95	|------------------------|------------------------|----------------------|
     96	| Yes | Yes | `Measured`: the `NVRM: Xid` count in the window is real, including 0 |
     97	| Yes | No | `Not observable`: the pipeline ships other logs but not kernel messages |
     98	| No (empty hours in the window) | Any | `Not observable` for the empty hours. List them |
     99	| No stream for the instance | n/a | `Not observable` |
     100	
     101	- Evaluate every source separately. One live source is enough for `Measured`, but
     102	  report dead sources too, because the operator probably thinks they work.
     103	- Identical counts from different nodes in the same query set usually mean identical
     104	  boot output from the same AMI, not live logging. Check the hourly bins.
     105	- Coverage is a point-in-time verdict. Late delivery can fill a gap later, and a
     106	  stopped shipper can resume. State the query time in the report, and if a gap ends
     107	  shortly before the query, say so rather than assuming the data is permanently lost.
     108	- For `Not observable`, tell the operator to check the node directly with
     109	  `dmesg -T | grep -i nvrm` or `journalctl -k | grep -i xid`, and to fix log shipping.
     110	  Never report it as "no GPU errors".
     111	- Check the Logs Insights `statistics` too. `recordsScanned = 0` on query (a) has two
     112	  causes: the query is wrong (group, region, time range), or the source has no events
     113	  in the window. Query (b) is the control. If (b) returns rows for the same group and
     114	  instance, the query is right and the kernel stream is empty for the window
     115	  (`Not observable`). If (b) is also empty, fix the query before concluding anything.
     116	
     117	Other `NVRM:` lines that are not `NVRM: Xid` are driver diagnostics, not Xids. List
     118	them in the timeline if they cluster around the failure, but do not classify them with
     119	the Xid table or name them a root cause without corroborating evidence."}], "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_MbXcXbSfX36n5l70iAk8Ew", "content": [{"text": "     1	# NVIDIA Xid Triage Reference
     2	
     3	Source: [NVIDIA Xid catalog](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/xid-errors/analyzing-xid-catalog.html).
     4	Descriptions and action buckets below are taken from that catalog. The "Class" column
     5	is this skill's grouping of NVIDIA's action buckets for root-cause routing. Always
     6	prefer the catalog if it has been updated.
     7	
     8	Xids appear in the kernel log as `NVRM: Xid (PCI:<bus-id>): <code>, ...`. On HyperPod
     9	they are surfaced in the `SagemakerHealthMonitoringAgent` log stream inside the HMA
     10	detection message. On ParallelCluster they appear in the `system-messages` or `syslog`
     11	stream of `/aws/parallelcluster/<cluster>-<timestamp>`. On self-managed fleets they
     12	appear only in whatever log group the customer ships the system log to. See SKILL.md
     13	Step 3a for discovery and the coverage check.
     14	
     15	An absent Xid is only meaningful when kernel logging for that node is proven live.
     16	`Not observable` and `0 Xids` are different findings.
     17	
     18	## Commonly seen codes
     19	
     20	NVIDIA catalog values (description, immediate action) as checked. Where an AWS page gives
     21	a different first step, the AWS step is listed because it is specific to EC2.
     22	
     23	| Xid | NVIDIA description | NVIDIA immediate action | Verdict for this skill |
     24	|-----|--------------------|-------------------------|------------------------|
     25	| 13 | Graphics Engine Exception | RESTART_APP | Application: LEAVE ALONE (unless paired with a hardware Xid) |
     26	| 31 | GPU memory page fault | RESTART_APP | Application: LEAVE ALONE (unless paired with a hardware Xid) |
     27	| 43 | GPU stopped processing | IGNORE | Sympathetic: follow the Xid that preceded it |
     28	| 45 | Preemptive cleanup, due to previous errors | WORKFLOW_XID_45 | Sympathetic: follow the other Xid |
     29	| 46 | GPU stopped processing | RESET_GPU | REBOOT; REPLACE if it recurs |
     30	| 48 | Double Bit ECC Error | WORKFLOW_XID_48 (solo: RESET_GPU; with 63 or 64: DRAIN_AND_RESET) | REBOOT (AWS: a reboot retires the page or activates remapped rows); REPLACE if 64 or a remap failure follows, or it recurs |
     31	| 62 | Internal micro-controller halt | RESET_GPU | REBOOT; REPLACE if it recurs |
     32	| 63 | GPU memory remapping event | IGNORE | MONITOR alone. After a 48, a remap is pending: REBOOT to activate it |
     33	| 64 | GPU memory remapping failure | RESET_GPU | REPLACE (AWS: remap failure needs stop/start to move to healthy hardware) |
     34	| 74 | NVLINK Error | WORKFLOW_NVLINK_ERR | REBOOT; REPLACE if it recurs |
     35	| 79 | GPU has fallen off the bus | RESTART_BM | REBOOT first (AWS); stop/start (REPLACE) if it persists |
     36	| 92 | High single-bit ECC error rate | IGNORE | MONITOR; watch for 48/64 |
     37	| 94 | Contained memory error | RESTART_APP | LEAVE ALONE (contained); MONITOR |
     38	| 95 | Uncontained memory error | RESET_GPU | REBOOT; REPLACE if it recurs |
     39	| 109 | Context Switch Timeout Error | RESET_GPU | REBOOT; REPLACE if it recurs |
     40	| 110 | Security Fault Error | RESET_GPU | REBOOT; investigate software |
     41	| 119 | GSP RPC Timeout | RESET_GPU | Driver configuration: AWS says these occur with GSP activated and the fix is to deactivate GSP. A reboot alone does not stop recurrence. Verdict LEAVE ALONE with the GSP action |
     42	| 120 | GSP Error | RESET_GPU | Same as 119 |
     43	| 136 | Link Training Failed | RESET_GPU | REBOOT; REPLACE if it recurs |
     44	| 140 | ECC Unrecovered Error | RESET_GPU | REBOOT; REPLACE if it recurs |
     45	| 143 | GPU Initialization Error | RESET_GPU | REBOOT; REPLACE if it recurs |
     46	| 151 | Key rotation Error | RESTART_VM | REBOOT |
     47	| 154 | GPU Recovery Action Changed | XID_154 (informational, about another Xid) | Use its value, see rule 7 |
     48	| 155 | NVLINK: SW Defined Error | RESET_GPU (investigatory: INVESTIGATE_SW_USER) | Software-defined link event: REBOOT only if links stay down; not a hardware verdict on its own |
     49	| 156 | Resource Retirement Event | RESET_GPU (investigatory: IGNORE) | MONITOR |
     50	| 158 | GPU Fatal Timeout | RESET_GPU | REBOOT; REPLACE if it recurs |
     51	
     52	Note on conflicting sources: the Amazon ECS GPU auto repair page lists 155 as "GPU NVLink
     53	flit CRC error" and 156 as "GPU NVLink lane error". The NVIDIA catalog describes them as
     54	above. Follow NVIDIA, and say the sources differ if the verdict depends on it.
     55	
     56	Other GPU memory signals that are not Xids ([AWS Xid troubleshooting](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/ec2-linux-troubleshoot-xid-errors)):
     57	
     58	| Signal | Where | Verdict |
     59	|--------|-------|---------|
     60	| `WARNING: infoROM is corrupted at gpu` | Kernel log (does not match `NVRM: Xid`) | REBOOT; stop/start (REPLACE) if it persists |
     61	| `Remapped Rows ... Pending: Yes` | `nvidia-smi -q` on the node | REBOOT (GPU reset required) |
     62	| `Remapping Failure Occurred: Yes` | `nvidia-smi -q` on the node | REPLACE (stop/start) |
     63	| `Pending Page Blacklist: Yes` (older GPUs) | `nvidia-smi -q` on the node | REBOOT |
     64	| Fewer GPUs than the instance type has | Distinct `GpuId` (`AWS/EC2`) or `index` (`CWAgent`) dimension values from `ListMetrics`, compared with `DescribeInstanceTypes` GPU count; on the node, `nvidia-smi --list-gpus` | REPLACE (AWS: stop and start). Missing metrics are Not observable, never a low count |
     65	
     66	## Routing rules
     67	
     68	1. **Order matters.** Sort Xids by time per node. The first non-sympathetic Xid is the
     69	   candidate cause; later 43/45 entries are usually consequences.
     70	2. **Hardware class on one node, job failed after:** branch A. Recommend replacing that
     71	   node (not reboot) if the same hardware-class Xid recurs after a reboot.
     72	3. **Application class on many nodes at once, no hardware class anywhere:** branch F.
     73	   Suspect code, input data, or framework version.
     74	4. **119/120 on multiple nodes after an AMI or driver change:** branch E. Correlate with
     75	   `UpdateClusterSoftware` or `CurrentImageId` changes.
     76	5. **63 alone** is not a root cause. Do not report it as one.

     78	   `Xid 154 GPU recovery action changed from 0x0 (None) to 0x2 (Node Reboot Required)`.
     79	   Values: `None`, `Drain P2P`, `Drain and Reset`, `GPU Reset Required`, `Node Reboot Required`.
     80	   `GPU Reset Required` or `Node Reboot Required` means REBOOT for the node it names.
     81	8. **Unknown code:** report the raw code and message, mark the classification
     82	   `UNVERIFIED`, and link the NVIDIA catalog. Do not guess.

     7	## 1. Which transport NCCL actually used
     8	
     9	NCCL writes its transport choices only when `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` (or higher) is set, and only
     10	to the job's stdout or to `NCCL_DEBUG_FILE`. These reach CloudWatch only if the customer
     11	ships job output. Search every log source found in SKILL.md Step 3a for `NCCL INFO` and

     15	| Log line | Meaning | Verdict |
     16	|----------|---------|---------|
     17	| `NET/OFI Selected Provider is efa` and `Using network AWS Libfabric` | Inter-node traffic goes over EFA through the AWS OFI NCCL plugin | Good |
     18	| `Using network IB` | NCCL chose an InfiniBand-verbs network | Unexpected on EC2 EFA instances; report it |
     19	| Channel lines `... via NET/Socket/<n>` | Inter-node traffic over TCP sockets | **Bad** on EFA instances: silent fallback. The AWS blog on P3dn measured about a three-fold bus-bandwidth gain for EFA over TCP |
     20	| Channel lines `... via P2P/CUMEM` | Intra-node GPU to GPU by direct peer access (NVLink on NVSwitch nodes) | Good |
     21	| `NVLS Creating Multicast group ...` | NVLink SHARP in use for collectives | Good on NVSwitch systems that support it |
     22	| Channel lines `... via SHM/direct/direct` | Intra-node traffic through host shared memory | On an NVSwitch node, peer access is not being used; report as degraded |
     23	
     24	Sources: [NCCL logging](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/nccl/user-guide/docs/troubleshooting/logging.html),

     32	## 2. NVLink and NVSwitch fabric

     34	The CloudWatch agent's NVIDIA plugin does **not** collect any NVLink counter (its full

     36	NVLink health reaches AWS only through the system log:

     2	name: aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation
     3	description: Use this skill for GPU training or inference clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or
     4	  EKS), ParallelCluster, or self-managed EC2/EKS GPU instances. It adds three things.

     9	  headlined as hardware. Third, a pre-flight readiness check before a long run, covering

     12	  GPUs. Activate on Xid or ECC errors, slow training or FSx for Lustre slowness on a GPU

     15	metadata:
     16	  author: nzuresh
     17	  version: "1.0.0"
     18	  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: "Incident RCA, Chat tasks"
     19	  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: "Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, AWS ParallelCluster, Amazon EC2, Amazon FSx for Lustre, Elastic Fabric Adapter, Amazon EKS, AWS Health"
     20	  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: "Machine Learning, GenAI, High Performance Computing"
     21	---
     22	
     23	# GPU Cluster Evidence, Readiness, and Fault Verdicts
     24	
     25	For GPU clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or EKS), AWS ParallelCluster, and self-managed
     26	EC2 or EKS. Generic investigation finds the obvious signals; this skill adds what it gets
     27	wrong: silent evidence, wrong-headline hardware verdicts, and predictable failures before a
     28	long run. **Read-only.** Never reboot, replace, update, or delete anything, and never read
     29	training data, checkpoints, or model weights.
     30	
     31	## Critical rules R1 to R10 (apply in every mode, in this order)
     32	
     33	R1. **Answer in one pass.** In chat, do not stop to ask a question and do not hand off to a
     34	   separate investigation before answering. If an input is missing, use the default (impact
     35	   window: last 24 hours; run length: evaluate 24, 48, and 72 hours), state the assumption,
     36	   and mark dependent checks `Needs input`. For "slow" or performance questions with no
     37	   time given, use the last 72 hours. Offer follow-ups only after the answer.
     38	R2. **Inventory and capability profile.** HyperPod: `sagemaker.DescribeCluster` and
     39	   `ListClusterNodes` (paginate). EC2/ParallelCluster/EKS: `ec2.DescribeInstances`. For every
     40	   GPU instance type: `ec2.DescribeInstanceTypes` (strip HyperPod `ml.`): GPU count,
     41	   `EfaSupported`, `MaximumEfaInterfaces`; per EC2 node, attached `efa`/`efa-only` interfaces.
     42	   Report `<attached> of <max>`, where attached = interfaces with `InterfaceType` `efa` or
     43	   `efa-only` (the primary ENA interface does not count unless it is `efa`). HyperPod nodes
     44	   are not visible to `DescribeInstances`: say so. On NVSwitch types, search every log source
     45	   found under rule R4 for `Started "Nvidia Fabric Manager"` before saying it is not confirmed.
     46	R3. **Node identity survives replacement.** A HyperPod reboot keeps the instance ID; a replace
     47	   gives the node a **new instance ID in the same instance group**, so the current ID will
     48	   never appear in the replace request. Query CloudTrail **by event name, not by instance
     49	   ID**: `cloudtrail.LookupEvents` with `LookupAttributes=[{AttributeKey: EventName,
     50	   AttributeValue: BatchReplaceClusterNodes}]`, then again for `BatchRebootClusterNodes`,
     51	   `BatchDeleteClusterNodes`, and `UpdateCluster`, with `StartTime` = window start minus 6
     52	   hours and `EndTime` = now as full ISO-8601 UTC timestamps, paginating with `NextToken`.
     53	   Keep events whose `requestParameters.clusterName` is this cluster. A `nodeIds` entry
     54	   that is not in the current `ListClusterNodes` output was replaced; the instance group
     55	   whose node has a `LaunchTime` just after that event is the replaced group. That operator
     56	   or automatic call is the explanation for the node going `Pending` (Branch E), not hardware.
     57	R4. **Find every log source by substring, not prefix.** Call `logs.DescribeLogGroups` with
     58	   `logGroupNamePattern` (case-sensitive substring) = the cluster name, then again for
     59	   `kernel`, `messages`, `syslog`, `journal`, and `gpu`, paginating with `nextToken`. Never
     60	   search only `/aws/parallelcluster` or `/aws/sagemaker` prefixes: customer pipelines use
     61	   other names (for example `/aws/<pipeline>/<cluster>/kernel`). Evaluate every source found.
     62	R5. **Prove coverage before any "no errors".** For each node and source: find the stream that
     63	   carries `kernel:` lines, then bin **that exact stream** by hour across the window padded by
     64	   one hour. **Always name the evidence you used: quote the full log group name and the exact
     65	   log stream name for every node in the coverage table, and again in the answer text.** A
     66	   coverage claim without the group and stream it rests on is not auditable, so the operator
     67	   cannot re-run it. Any empty hour means `Not observable` for that hour. First and last event times
     68	   are not proof, and the time of the **last `kernel:` line** is not when logging stopped:
     69	   a healthy kernel goes quiet. Liveness comes only from the hourly bins of all lines in
     70	   that stream. A node is `Measured` if one source passes. HyperPod: a missing
     71	   `SagemakerHealthMonitoringAgent/<group>/<instance-id>` stream means `No HMA detections`
     72	   when the cluster log group is otherwise live. NCCL transport with no `NCCL INFO` lines
     73	   anywhere is `Not observable`; never infer it from the instance type.
     74	R6. **Verdict per node, headline to match.** `REPLACE`, `REBOOT`, `LEAVE ALONE`, `MONITOR`, or
     75	   `NOT OBSERVABLE`, against the evidence bar in `references/incident-branches.md` (Step 4b).
     76	   Application-class Xids (for example 13, 31) or HMA `reason: XidUserAppError` with the node
     77	   `Running` is `LEAVE ALONE`. Never headline "hardware error" unless the verdict is `REPLACE`
     78	   or `REBOOT` on hardware grounds.
     79	R7. **Label every cause** `Proven` (measured signal on the affected node, before the failure,
     80	   nothing competing) or `Hypothesis (to validate)` with the one confirming measurement. A
     81	   spike at the same time is correlation. FSx without a saturated metric is not a proven cause.
     82	   Only a `Proven` cause may be called the root cause, in the headline or in a branch table.
     83	   Otherwise write `Leading hypothesis: <cause>`, or `Root cause: Not observable` when the
     84	   deciding evidence is missing (for example a dead control-plane log). Never write "Proven
     85	   mechanism" for something whose trigger or removal path you did not observe.
     86	   Utilization metrics from FSx (`NetworkThroughputUtilization`, `DiskIopsUtilization`, and
     87	   similar) and `GPUPowerUtilization` are already percent from 0 to 100: a value of `0.9` is
     88	   0.9 percent. Quote the raw value with a percent sign.
     89	R8. **Recovery questions** always state three things: whether automatic node recovery is on
     90	   (`NodeRecovery`), what it does (reboot or replace the node), and that the **job** resumes
     91	   only with checkpoints plus the orchestrator's auto-resume (Slurm on HyperPod:
     92	   `srun --auto-resume=1`).
     93	R9. **Capacity Blocks** begin terminating instances 30 minutes before the end time (60 for
     94	   UltraServers); blocks end at 11:30 UTC and termination starts at 11:00 UTC on the last day.
     95	   For a planned run, write out: usable until = end time minus the lead time; run end = start
     96	   plus run length; hours covered = usable until minus start. Give every value as a full UTC
     97	   date and time, and check the latest safe start is not already in the past.
     98	R10. **Rule out the frequent non-GPU causes** in `references/cluster-edge-cases.md` before
     99	   blaming hardware: subnet IP or network interface exhaustion, ParallelCluster bootstrap
     100	   failures and protected mode, EFA nodes in a public subnet, a Capacity Block not yet
     101	   active, and the FSx maintenance window. HyperPod does not export system metrics to
     102	   CloudWatch, so HyperPod GPU activity is `Not observable` there.
     103

     105	
     106	| The user asks | Mode | Steps to run |
     107	|---------------|------|--------------|

     109	| "Were there GPU errors?", "Can I trust the logs?" | **C: Coverage audit** | Steps 1 to 3, then 6 and 7 |
     110	| "Is the cluster ready for a long run?", Capacity Block ending | **P: Pre-flight** | Steps 1 to 3, then 5P, 6 and 7 |

     113	
     114	Work through these in order and tick each one as it completes. Skip only the steps the
     115	mode table excludes. Every step below has a matching `## Step N` section with its detail.

     135	[references/cluster-edge-cases.md](references/cluster-edge-cases.md) for the frequent non-GPU
     136	causes to rule out under rule R10:

     141	```

     143	Build one ordered timeline for the window plus 30 minutes each side: node state, HMA
     144	detections, Xids, AWS Health, EC2 status and scheduled events, Capacity Block and training plan
     145	end times, and CloudTrail cluster changes (rule R3).
     146	
     147	## Step 3: Coverage audit
     148	
     149	Load [references/coverage-audit.md](references/coverage-audit.md) for the log-source discovery
     150	and hourly coverage queries, and
     151	[references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md](references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md) for NCCL transport, NVLink and
     152	NVSwitch, and EFA signals:

     156	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md")

     160	Every row names the full log group name and the exact log stream name that row's verdict rests
     161	on, so the operator can re-run the same query. Where no stream carries kernel lines, say which
